text:
lucy: Heads-up — noticed something that's tripping up new users in the sample app: the Go SDK surfaces a generic "Error: auth failed" for 403, while Python returns PermissionDeniedError.

raj: Ugh yeah that's bad. We should have a consistent intent -> status -> typed-exception mapping. 401 vs 403 need different retry hints. 401 -> refresh credentials, 403 -> check scopes/role.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: introduce three canonical intents: authentication, authorization, rate_limit. Map them to typed exceptions AuthenticationError, PermissionDenied, RateLimitError. Keep HTTP code mapping separate but deterministic.

marta: For parity we also need the same names across SDKs. I prefer names that are language-idiomatic but same semantic token. E.g. Python: AuthenticationError, Go: AuthenticationError (type) or authentication_error (pkg).

owen: Quick implementation sketch (from SDK side):
```
// pseudo-Go error mapper
switch resp.StatusCode {
 case 401:
  return &errors.AuthenticationError{Msg: "token invalid or expired", Retryable: true}
 case 403:
  return &errors.PermissionDenied{Msg: "insufficient scope"}
 case 429:
  return &errors.RateLimit{Msg: "quota exceeded", RetryAfter: resp.Header.Get("Retry-After")}
 default:
  return &errors.Internal{Msg: "upstream error"}
}
```

raj: Love the sketch. Two extra asks: 1) message copy should include an actionable hint (one-liner) and 2) telemetry signal (error_code + intent) so ops can alert on authorization spikes.

lucy: +1. For onboarding docs, sample app should show exactly the user-visible message and the suggested fix. Right now examples show stack traces instead which is noisy.

sam: UX suggestion for messages: short neutral headline + one actionable bullet. Eg:
"Permission denied: missing scope 'inference.write'. Check your role or use the 'inference:write' policy."

marta: On the SDK/HTTP mapping table in the docs we should add a column "what to show to users" vs "what to log/telemetry". Different audiences.

owen: Also call out idempotency: some 409s are user errors vs write-conflicts. We should avoid lumping them into generic ClientError. Make ConflictError explicit.

lucy: Does everyone agree we should land a thin compatibility shim in the hosted API layer that normalizes some upstream noisy codes (e.g., upstream 403 with body {"reason":"rate_limit"}) so SDKs can rely on consistent semantics?

raj: +1 from security POV as long as we add trace id and original payload to the logs.

sam: I'll draft a short PR template for SDKs with the mapping table, sample messages, and telemetry fields. Can we include a sampleapp snippet showing how to catch and present the typed errors? Eg: 
```
try {
  client.Generate(...)
} catch (PermissionDenied e) {
  ui.Show("Permission denied: check your API key scopes. See docs")
}
```

marta: Nice. One more onboarding friction: the web quickstart auto-creates an API key with minimal scopes, so new users hit 403 immediately if they try write paths. We should either expand default scopes for first-run or surface a clearer CTA to upgrade scopes.

lucy: Good catch. Let's do clarity in quickstart and also add the explicit error example in the sampleapp README.

devex-bot: Ticket created: DEVEX-1873 "Unify SDK error intents+copy across languages" assigned to @sam, @marta. https://tickets.example/DEVEX-1873 :white_check_mark:

sam: I'll own the ticket. Timeline: draft PR + sampleapp patch this sprint, SDKs to follow next sprint. Will ping each SDK owner individually.

owen: If you want a fast win: add a central error-format doc under /docs/error-mapping.md, then SDKs can link to it.

lucy: Perfect. Thanks all — this should cut down on Support tickets from new teams. :thumbsup:
